articles.title: Man moved from Australia to Ferndale in Welsh valleys because it is so cheap
articles.summary: The area has attracted investors and even a buyer from Australia, but locals struggle to afford homes.
articles.body:
A house-hunter has moved 10,000 miles (16,000km) from Australia to Wales' most affordable town because the properties are so cheap.

James Brown, 56, spotted the three-bed house in Tylorstown, near Ferndale, Rhondda Cynon Taf, online for £80,000 and put an offer in.

"It's ideal if you're commuting, and everything's virtually on your doorstep, so a really affordable area to come to," he said.

But some people who live in Ferndale - dubbed Wales' most affordable town with an average property price of £116,200 - say they are still struggling to buy homes.

Zoopla says a typical home in Ferndale costs "less than twice the annual wages of two full-time workers".

The property selling website said its analysis shows this is the most affordable town in Wales.

Residents have described how they have had to travel to work in England to afford a home in the area, while an estate agent said the low prices attract investors and buy-to-rent landlords from outside south Wales.

Originally from Gloucester, when Brown moved back from Australia he decided to move to the south Wales valleys because of the property prices.

He said the equivalent property in his home region would have cost him £200,000.

Brown said: "It's definitely a lot of outside buyers buying properties in Wales which I suppose in some ways is not helping the local people get on the ladder, but like I said, the affordability is just unreal in south Wales."

Emma Weston, 36, who runs a café in Ferndale said she had to make the choice between using savings to invest in her business or buying a house.

"Obviously, I chose to keep my job and put the money here," she said.

My partner, he's an electrician, a good trade, I obviously manage a business.

"We still have money but there's nothing left in the pot whereby I can say we can save X-amount to put down to a deposit."

Weston knows property is more expensive elsewhere, but says Ferndale still does not feel affordable.

"I've lived outside of the valleys, therefore I can see the comparisons," she said.

"However, if you look at the cost of living crisis, which we're all facing, everything is just costing an absolute bomb."

Café customer Marcus, 31, took a job nearly 100 miles (165km) away in Somerset so he could afford a family home.

"Moving to my new job gave that opportunity to buy the house," he said.

Thomas said he liked the security of having his own home, and sees it as an investment for his children.

But he said: "I think if you were living in London, Reading... Birmingham... I'd say it is the easiest place to get a property because the house value here and there is completely different.

"For us, it's hard. For people coming into Wales is easy and is affordable."

Estate agent David Ricketts said the south Wales valleys are attractive to people outside the area.

"You're getting more for your money, there's less stress, there's a lower mortgage to pay and it's an area which I think will get better and better, it'll grow and you'd get a lovely welcome in any valleys town," he said.

Ricketts said some buyers were not necessarily looking to live there themselves.

"What you've got now is a situation, not only just to buy, you have investors coming in because they've realised that the rental yield is quite reasonable and that will only grow," he said.

"These are very attractive areas to live and also to be a landlord."

Donna Thomas, 41, rents in Maerdy with her partner and their three children.

They rent because a mortgage is too expensive.

"If we're happy where we are, why change that? Why go into an even more stressful situation rather than just stay where we are and make do with what we have?

"It would be more stress, and everything would be harder, the money wouldn't stretch as far and the thing is we want to give the girls the best life that we possibly can with what we have," she said.

Thomas said she was happy for investors to buy properties in the area and rent them back to locals.

She said: "It means that when you can't afford to get a mortgage on a house that you really like, if somebody else did buy it, and then rented it out to you, I would say that would be really good.

"I think I can't afford to get a mortgage on this house, but I really like this house, and now I'm renting it."

Chiropractor Ellie Thomas, 25, lives with her parents in Ferndale.

She is saving up for a deposit on a house near a city.

"I don't think I would want to live here," she said.

"I just feel like there's not much going on here. Most of the shops are shut. There's like one café, a few hairdressers, there's not really much."

However, she understands it was likely to be more expensive and harder to buy elsewhere.

"Obviously, it's a bit hard to find somewhere nice in the area you want for an affordable price," she said.

"It would be easier for me to live here.

"It's a lovely community, everyone knows each other, but it's just a bit far out of the way, and petrol is expensive now too."

articles.title: Casa do Papai Noel em Ceilândia fecha após 24 anos de tradição | G1
articles.standfirst: Toninho, idealizador da casa, explica que questões de saúde e roubos frequentes motivaram decisão de encerrar atividades.
articles.summary: Toninho, idealizador da casa, explica que questões de saúde e roubos frequentes motivaram decisão de encerrar atividades.
articles.body:
Depois de 24 anos recebendo visitas de famílias em dezembro, a Casa do Papai Noel em Ceilândia , no Distrito Federal, encerrou suas atividades .

🎅 O local foi cuidado por Toninho , idealizador da casa, e Marinalva Reis , sua ex-esposa e parceira de vida, responsável pela decoração interna.

🎄 A casa funcionava por quase todo o mês de dezembro, com visitas gratuitas, proporcionando uma imersão natalina. Pelos cálculos do Toninho, cerca de 3 mil pessoas passavam para visitar todos os anos.

Toninho explica que questões de saúde e os roubos frequentes contra a casa levaram a decisão de encerrar as atividades.

"Saúde em primeiro lugar. Vou fazer 70 anos ano que vem, dona Marinalva também, 71. Tivemos assalto à mão armada, com revólver na cabeça. Bens a gente recuperou, depois acharam meu carro, menos mal. Mas um problema constante que a gente tinha, porque eu fazia a armação toda do lado de fora com fiação, roubavam no outro dia, tinha que sair e comprar tudo. Fiz uma cirurgia recente. E aí nós resolvemos", conta Toninho.

Toninho, idealizador e responsável pela Casa do Papai Noel — Foto: TV Globo

Toninho explica que a saudade de sua mãe, que já faleceu, foi uma das razões para se dedicar à decoração da casa . Ela fazia aniversário no dia 24 de dezembro e gostava de comemorar com os filhos na ceia de Natal.

"Era obrigação nossa, no dia 24, estar com a casa toda enfeitada para poder cear com ela meia noite, em função do aniversário dela e comemorar o nascimento de Cristo. Ela amava Natal e era espírita, arrecadava alimentos, brinquedo para crianças", diz.

Toninho diz que, após o falecimento da mãe, continuou se dedicando ao Natal.

"O sonho dela, através do centro espírita, era construir uma creche para 60 crianças. Nós começamos a trazer as creches para entregar brinquedo, para entregar presente", conta Toninho.

Marinalva conta que as crianças das creches recebiam lanches, aconchego e brinquedos.

Marinalva Reis, ex-esposa de Toninho, cuidava da decoração interna da Casa do Papai Noel — Foto: TV Globo

Marinalva diz que cada cantinho da casa estava enfeitado para o Natal. A máquina de neve fazia sucesso entre as crianças.

"O quarto, a copa, a sala, a cozinha. Cada ano, eu sempre criei uma coisa diferente. Fazia com muita alegria, muito amor mesmo. Sempre valorizei esse projeto dele", diz Marinalva Reis.

Com o encerramento das atividades, a decoração da casa vai alegrar o natal de outras pessoas. Toninho e Marinalva fizeram um bazar para liquidar os artigos natalinos, como guirlandas, pratos, toalhas, potes e pisca-piscas.

"Fica aquela nostalgia, saudade, mas fica também a satisfação de dever cumprido", fala Marinalva.

articles.title: Acidentes de trânsito em Manaus: 196 atendimentos no fim de semana | G1
articles.standfirst: Hospitais e Prontos-Socorros (HPS) da capital receberam 123 pacientes durante os dois dias, o equivalente a 62,7% do total de atendimentos. Foram 67 registros no sábado e 56 no domingo.
articles.summary: Acidentes de trânsito em Manaus deixaram 196 feridos no fim de semana, com motociclistas somando 83% das ocorrências nos hospitais Platão Araújo e João Lúcio.
articles.body:
Motocicleta da vítima após colisão com micro-ônibus — Foto: Divulgação

Manaus registrou 196 atendimentos hospitalares por acidentes de trânsito entre sábado (21) e domingo (22), segundo dados da Secretaria de Estado de Saúde do Amazonas (SES-AM). Os acidentes com motocicletas concentraram a maior parte das ocorrências, com 164 casos, o que corresponde a 83,6% do total.

Além dos acidentes de moto, foram registrados 17 atendimentos por acidentes de carro, 12 por outros tipos de ocorrências no trânsito e três atropelamentos.

Os dados mostram ainda uma redução de 32,4% no número de atendimentos de um dia para o outro. No sábado, foram 117 entradas hospitalares. Já no domingo, o total caiu para 79.

No sábado, 107 vítimas atendidas se envolveram em acidentes de moto, seis em acidentes de carro, duas foram atropeladas e outras duas deram entrada por diferentes ocorrências de trânsito.

A maior parte dos atendimentos ocorreu entre 0h e 12h, período que registrou 76 casos, contra 41 entre 13h e 24h. Os horários com mais ocorrências foram às 5h e às 11h, com 10 atendimentos cada.

No domingo, dos 79 atendimentos registrados, 57 foram por acidentes de moto, 11 por acidentes de carro, 10 por outras ocorrências de trânsito e um por atropelamento.

Diferentemente do sábado, o domingo teve maior concentração de atendimentos no período da tarde e da noite. Entre 13h e 24h, foram registrados 49 casos, enquanto entre 0h e 12h houve 30 atendimentos. O horário com maior número de ocorrências foi às 16h, quando 16 pessoas deram entrada em unidades de saúde.

Hospitais e prontos-socorros receberam a maioria das vítimas

Os Hospitais e Prontos-Socorros (HPS) da capital receberam 123 pacientes durante os dois dias, o equivalente a 62,7% do total de atendimentos. Foram 67 registros no sábado e 56 no domingo.

Já os Serviços de Pronto Atendimento (SPA) e as Unidades de Pronto Atendimento (UPA) atenderam 70 vítimas, sendo 49 no sábado e 21 no domingo. Os Hospitais e Prontos-Socorros da Criança (HPSC) registraram três atendimentos no período.

Entre as unidades de saúde, os maiores volumes de atendimento foram registrados no HPS Platão Araújo, com 62 casos, e no HPS Dr. João Lúcio, com 61.

Na sequência aparecem a UPA José Rodrigues, com 26 atendimentos, e o SPA Eliameme Mady, com 16. O SPA e Policlínica Dr. José Lins registrou nove casos, enquanto o SPA e Policlínica Danilo Corrêa contabilizou oito atendimentos.

O SPA Joventina Dias atendeu cinco vítimas, todas no sábado. Já o SPA Zona Sul registrou quatro atendimentos. O HPSC Zona Leste recebeu dois pacientes no domingo, e o SPA Coroado registrou uma ocorrência no sábado.

articles.title: Supercélula em Tupanciretã: Homem grava destruição de cidade no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Fenômeno classificado como supercélula atingiu a cidade da Região Central do RS na sexta-feira (20). Morador de Caxias do Sul que visitava familiares teve o veículo atingido por granizo e escombros.
articles.summary: Com ventos de 114 km/h, a supercélula em Tupanciretã deixou cinco mortos e rastro de destruição registrado em vídeo por turista que teve o veículo atingido por escombros.
articles.body:
Um turista que presenciou a tempestade com ventos de 114 km/h que devastou Tupanciretã , na Região Central do Rio Grande do Sul, durante o feriado de sexta-feira (20) relata que viveu momentos de tensão. Ele e a família se abrigaram durante o temporal que destelhou uma igreja, destruiu veículos e causou danos em milhares de residências . Cinco pessoas morreram e 265 ficaram feridas .

⛈️ Meteorologistas apontam que o município foi atingido por uma supercélula . As supercélulas são grandes nuvens de tempestade que se desenvolvem tanto horizontalmente quanto verticalmente. Elas podem provocar rajadas acima de 90 km/h, grandes volumes de chuva em pouco tempo, granizo, microexplosões e até tornados.

O representante comercial Cristiano Gasperin, morador de Caxias do Sul , cidade da Serra Gaúcha a quase 400 km de Tupanciretã, passava o feriado prolongado na casa dos sogros.

"O telhado parecia que levantava e baixava. Era um estrondo muito forte. E aí começaram as pedras"

Tempestade com vento e granizo deixa rastro de destruição em Tupanciretã — Foto: Imagens cedidas/Cristiano Gasperin

Ele registrou em vídeo o momento em que a ventania atingiu o município . "Eu fiz aquele vídeo, que eu até acabei divulgando, às 3h30. Demorou cerca de meia hora, mais ou menos, até acalmar."

Nas gravações, é possível observar o momento em que a igreja perdeu todo o telhado . O carro de Gasperin, que estava estacionado do outro lado da rua, ficou destruído após ser atingido por pedras de granizo e pela torre da igreja.

Durante a madrugada, a família precisou buscar abrigo no andar inferior da residência . "Estava dormindo, era três da manhã, onde a gente desceu pra se resguardar", relatou Gasperin.

"A gente percebe a dimensão do estrago e a força do vento, justamente com a cúpula da igreja que caiu, além daquela pilastra que ficou em pé, que é a outra do outro lado, e a torre um pouquinho maior, de tudo destruído", afirma o representante comercial.

A casa dos familiares também foi atingida pelo temporal, e amigos organizaram um mutirão para auxiliar na recuperação do imóvel .

Sobre o momento da tempestade, Gasperin descreve a tensão vivida:

"Uma sensação de impotência, né? Porque tu não tem o que fazer, o negócio é se proteger, esperar passar, passar e depois a gente vê, quando acalmou a gente saiu para a rua e viu a proporção de tudo", diz.

articles.title: Juiz de Fora registra 16 ocorrências após chuva de mais de 76 mm | G1
articles.standfirst: Entre as ocorrências estão alagamentos, escorregamentos de talude, desabamentos de muros e destelhamento. Impactos das chuvas foram observados em diferentes bairros da cidade.
articles.summary: Após chuva em Juiz de Fora de 76 mm, a Defesa Civil atendeu 16 ocorrências, incluindo desabamentos e alagamentos nos bairros Industrial, Fontesville e Ipiranga.
articles.body:
A Defesa Civil de Juiz de Fora atendeu 16 ocorrências após as chuvas que atingiram a cidade entre a noite de domingo (22) e a madrugada desta segunda-feira (23). Segundo o pluviômetro do Dom Orione, na região Oeste, o volume acumulado da água chegou a 76,5 milímetros .

Entre os registros estão alagamentos, escorregamentos de talude, desabamentos de muros e destelhamento parcial de imóvel . Os impactos das chuvas foram observados em diferentes regiões da cidade.

Na Zona Norte , a Defesa Civil atendeu alagamentos nos bairros Amazônia e Esplanada ,e três escorregamentos de talude em Santa Cruz e Cidade do Sol. Também houve ameaça de deslizamento de terra no Democrata .

No Fontesville , um muro de contenção de talude desabou e atingiu parte de uma residência. O Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionado para prestar atendimento aos moradores. A Defesa Civil esteve no local e realizou a interdição parcial do imóvel.

"O desabamento também atingiu dois botijões de gás, ocasionando vazamento com risco de explosão, que foi prontamente contido pelos militares", informou a assessoria dos bombeiros.

Bombeiros realizam atendimento após queda de muro de contenção de talude no Fontesville — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros

No Bairro Industrial, também na região Norte, o Córrego do Humaitá transbordou durante a noite de domingo. Diferentes vias continuavam alagadas na manhã desta segunda-feira.

Ruas amanheceram alagadas no Bairro Industrial — Foto: Foto: Sidney Euclides

Na Zona Sul da cidade, foram registrados alagamento no bairro Santa Efigênia , escorregamento de talude no Teixeiras e destelhamento parcial de um imóvel no São Mateus . A Defesa Ciivl também foi acionada para atender duas ameaças de deslizamento de terra em Santa Luzia e Santa Cecília.

Imagens gravadas por moradores do bairro Ipiranga , também na região Sul, mostram a rua Etiene Loures tomada pela água durante a noite de domingo. Veja o vídeo:

A equipe da Defesa Civil também esteve na Vila Olavo Costa , na região Sudeste, onde um muro desabou.

Volumes das chuvas nos bairros da cidade

De acordo com a Prefeitura de Juiz de Fora, outros pontos da cidade também tiveram volumes de chuva expressivos. Os maiores acumulados foram observados em:

São Judas Tadeu, na região Norte: 67,8 mm;

articles.title: Vertical Connect lança PYROS, aeronave elétrica para combater incêndio | G1
articles.standfirst: Com autonomia de até 1h30 e registro na Anac, o equipamento faz parte da expansão do portfólio da fabricante brasileira para o mercado de proteção ambiental e emergências.
articles.summary: Com autonomia de até 1h30 e registro na Anac, o equipamento faz parte da expansão do portfólio da fabricante brasileira para o mercado de proteção ambiental e emergências.
articles.body:
Vertical Connect lança PYROS, aeronave elétrica brasileira para combater incêndios — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação.

Desenvolvido em parceria com a Dakila Pesquisas, o eVTOL não tripulado tem alcance informado de até 100 km e deverá integrar um projeto pioneiro de resposta aérea a incêndios em uma cidade brasileira.

A fabricante brasileira Vertical Connect apresentou o PYROS, sua primeira aeronave elétrica desenvolvida especificamente para o combate a incêndios e o apoio a operações de emergência. O modelo combina decolagem e pouso vertical com um tanque de até 400 litros de água, configuração pensada para levar apoio aéreo a áreas de difícil acesso e complementar o trabalho das equipes em solo.

Segundo a fabricante, o PYROS tem peso máximo de decolagem de 750 kg, autonomia de até 1 hora e 30 minutos e alcance de até 100 km, conforme a configuração e o perfil da missão. Para uma jornada operacional de oito horas, a empresa estima que a aeronave possa atuar em uma área de até 450 hectares, dependendo do terreno, das condições meteorológicas e da logística de reabastecimento. O modelo possui registro na Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (ANAC) sob o número PR-832686709.

“Nós desenvolvemos o PYROS para responder a uma necessidade concreta de quem está na linha de frente. Quando o acesso por terra é difícil, ter uma aeronave capaz de levar até 400 litros de água ao ponto indicado pela equipe pode fazer diferença na resposta. O próximo passo é colocar essa tecnologia dentro da estrutura de atendimento dos municípios, junto de quem conhece o terreno e coordena a operação.” - José Carlos Más, fundador e CSO da Vertical Connect

O primeiro projeto municipal está em preparação. A proposta é integrar o PYROS às equipes de resposta locais, com planejamento de missões, pontos de reabastecimento e coordenação entre a aeronave e os profissionais em campo. A Vertical Connect afirma que a iniciativa foi concebida para ser a primeira do país a estruturar um sistema municipal de combate a incêndios com aeronaves elétricas não tripuladas. O nome da cidade será divulgado no anúncio oficial.

O lançamento amplia o portfólio da fabricante, que já desenvolveu o SKYROS para o agronegócio, o AËROS para a mobilidade aérea urbana e o ÜNICO para lazer e aviação esportiva. Com o PYROS, a empresa leva sua experiência em propulsão elétrica e decolagem vertical a um novo mercado, o de operações aéreas para proteção ambiental e resposta a emergências.

articles.title: Explosão de cilindro deixa cliente ferida e destruição em choperia | G1
articles.standfirst: Explosão ocorreu no estoque de bebidas do estabelecimento. Estilhaços atingiram a perna de uma cliente.
articles.summary: Explosão ocorreu no estoque de bebidas do estabelecimento. Estilhaços atingiram a perna de uma cliente.
articles.body:
Uma explosão de um cilindro de gás carbônico (CO₂) deixou uma cliente ferida e provocou estragos em uma choperia na Rua 14 de julho, região central de Campo Grande , na noite de domingo (22). Imagens feitas após o incidente mostram pedaços de tijolos espalhados pelo chão, objetos danificados e parte do estabelecimento destruída.

Segundo a choperia, o cilindro estava no estoque de bebidas quando explodiu. Com o impacto, estilhaços foram lançados e atingiram a perna de uma cliente, que sofreu ferimentos.

Em nota, a choperoa Madanela informou que uma possível falha no cilindro foi apontada preliminarmente pelo Corpo de Bombeiros, mas que as causas da explosão ainda serão apuradas. O estabelecimento também afirmou que todos estão bem e que retomaria o atendimento normal nesta segunda-feira (23). Veja a nota na íntegra ao final da reportagem.

O Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionado, prestou atendimento à vítima e isolou a área por segurança.

Local onde ocorreu a explosão — Foto: Reprodução

A empresa responsável pelo fornecimento do cilindro também se colocou à disposição para colaborar com a apuração.

As imagens mostram a dimensão dos estragos. Na área externa, o chão ficou coberto por tijolos e outros destroços. Dentro do estabelecimento, mesas e cadeiras aparecem em meio aos objetos espalhados pelo impacto.

Veja a nota da Chopperia Madalena na íntegra:

"A Chopperia Madalena informa que, na noite de ontem, ocorreu um incidente envolvendo um cilindro de CO₂ localizado no estoque de bebidas do estabelecimento, que acabou explodindo e ocasionando a projeção de estilhaços, atingindo a perna de uma cliente. A cliente sofreu ferimentos leves e recebeu prontamente atendimento do Corpo de Bombeiros, que esteve no local, prestou assistência e realizou o isolamento da área, seguindo os procedimentos de segurança. Felizmente, todos estão bem. Desde o ocorrido, estamos tomando as providências necessárias para apurar os fatos e esclarecer as circunstâncias do incidente. A empresa fornecedora do cilindro já se colocou à disposição para colaborar com a apuração e identificar as possíveis causas. Uma possível falha no equipamento foi apontada preliminarmente pelo Corpo de bombeiros mas os detalhes ainda serão apurados. Reforçamos nosso compromisso com a segurança, o cuidado com nossos clientes e a responsabilidade diante de qualquer situação. Estamos acompanhando de perto o caso e colaborando para que tudo seja devidamente esclarecido. Agradecemos a preocupação, as mensagens recebidas e a compreensão de todos. Equipe Chopperia Madalena."

articles.title: Nvidia anuncia volta de Jensen Huang ao comando da empresa | G1
articles.standfirst: Executivo havia renunciado em 12 de novembro, após revelações sobre relacionamento com empresária suspeita de espionagem para a China.
articles.summary: Executivo havia renunciado em 12 de novembro, após revelações sobre relacionamento com empresária suspeita de espionagem para a China.
articles.body:
Jensen Huang renunciou ao cargo em 12 de novembro. — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

A Nvidia anunciou nesta segunda-feira (23) o retorno de Jensen Huang ao cargo de presidente-executivo da companhia, com efeito imediato. Ele havia renunciado em 12 de novembro , após a revelação de um relacionamento extraconjugal com Alice Huang, empresária suspeita pelas autoridades americanas de envolvimento em atividades de espionagem para a China.

Após o anúncio, as ações da Nvidia dispararam quase 30% nas negociaçõe s antes da abertura das bolsas americanas. A notícia também impulsionou os contratos futuros do Nasdaq 100, índice que reúne grandes empresas de tecnologia dos Estados Unidos, que subiam 6,53% nesta segunda-feira.

A decisão representa uma reviravolta na posição do conselho de administração da Nvidia, que havia descartado a possibilidade de recontratar Huang poucos dias antes.

Segundo a gigante de tecnologia, a reintegração foi aprovada por unanimidade após uma série de reuniões com o executivo . O conselho afirmou estar satisfeito com a transparência de Huang e sua capacidade de voltar a liderar a empresa.

"O conselho acredita que Jensen é a pessoa certa para liderar a Nvidia e que seu retorno atende aos interesses de nossos acionistas, funcionários, parceiros e clientes", afirmou Harvey Jones, presidente do conselho de administração, em comunicado.

Jones também agradeceu a Colette Kress, que assumiu temporariamente o comando da companhia e continuará exercendo o cargo de diretora financeira. Ele permanecerá à frente do conselho.

A empresa informou ainda que consultou autoridades do alto escalão do governo americano antes de decidir pela reintegração.

"No processo de tomada de decisão, o conselho recebeu informações de altos funcionários do governo dos Estados Unidos e, com base nelas, está confiante de que o retorno de Huang não representa riscos à segurança nacional", afirmou.

Na noite de domingo (22), o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, havia pedido a volta do empresário ao comando da Nvidia . Em uma publicação nas redes sociais, Trump afirmou que a recontratação seria "a melhor coisa para a empresa e também para os Estados Unidos".

Alice Huang participando de um jantar organizado pelo CEO e cofundador da Nvidia. — Foto: AFP

Jensen Huang renunciou ao comando da Nvidia no mês passado, após a divulgação de relacionamentos extraconjugais , incluindo um com Alice Huang, empresária suspeita pelas autoridades americanas de envolvimento em atividades de espionagem para a China.

Uma investigação interna apontou que o executivo manteve relacionamentos amorosos não revelados com funcionárias da companhia, o que violaria as regras internas da empresa.

O caso ganhou repercussão após o jornal americano The New York Times revelar, em outubro, o relacionamento entre Huang e Alice.

Segundo a publicação, a empresária teria sido recrutada pela China para obter informações sobre o executivo e a Nvidia .

As suspeitas levantaram preocupações devido à importância da fabricante de chips na disputa tecnológica entre EUA e China, especialmente no desenvolvimento da inteligência artificial (IA).

Em uma mensagem enviada aos funcionários, obtida pela Reuters, Huang confirmou o relacionamento extraconjugal e assumiu responsabilidade por suas ações.

"Fui infiel à minha esposa. Minhas ações fizeram mal a ela e aos nossos filhos. Não há desculpa para o que fiz", escreveu.

O executivo também afirmou que não compartilhou informações confidenciais, segredos comerciais ou tecnologias da Nvidia. Ao anunciar sua saída, reconheceu que a permanência no cargo poderia prejudicar o foco da empresa em seus negócios.

Na semana passada, Huang se manifestou publicamente sobre a possibilidade de retornar ao comando da Nvidia. Em uma publicação na rede social X, agradeceu o apoio recebido e reconheceu os erros que levaram à sua renúncia.

"Não atendi aos padrões esperados de todos na Nvidia e cometi erros graves na minha vida pessoal. Causei problemas ao conselho de administração, o que lamento profundamente. Assumo integralmente meus erros", declarou.

O empresário também afirmou que estava comprometido em colaborar com a investigação independente conduzida pelo conselho e que vinha recebendo pedidos de funcionários, investidores, parceiros comerciais e clientes para reassumir o cargo.

"Se o conselho de administração decidir que meu retorno é do melhor interesse dos nossos acionistas, dos nossos funcionários, da empresa e dos Estados Unidos, será uma honra atender a esses pedidos e retornar como CEO", escreveu.

Fundador da Nvidia em 1993, Huang transformou a fabricante de chips para videogames em uma das empresas mais valiosas do mundo e líder no mercado de processadores para inteligência artificial.

articles.title: Former Icelandic PM says world’s great powers are flexing their muscles
articles.summary: Iceland’s former PM warns climate change remains an existential threat as global power politics sidelines action.
articles.body:
Iceland’s former prime minister says that although climate change has fallen lower down on the international political agenda, it remains an existential crisis.

Katrin Jakobsdottir says our warming world is not just a catastrophe for nature, but a health and security emergency that cannot be ignored.

Her country is on the front lines of that emergency, with the Arctic warming at four times the rate of the rest of the world. Almost all of Iceland’s glaciers are rapidly retreating – one was declared “dead” in 2019.

Jakobsdottir says it all comes at a time when the world’s biggest powers are flexing their muscles – and the politics of compromise are being squeezed out.

articles.title: Chuva e calor marcam semana em Cuiabá; veja a previsão | G1
articles.standfirst: Capital está sob alerta amarelo do Inmet; temperaturas podem chegar a 36°C nos primeiros dias, com previsão de trovoadas e aumento da umidade no fim da semana.
articles.summary: Capital está sob alerta amarelo do Inmet; temperaturas podem chegar a 36°C nos primeiros dias, com previsão de trovoadas e aumento da umidade no fim da semana.
articles.body:
Diante da previsão de chuva e trovoadas, a orientação é redobrar os cuidados durante os períodos de instabilidade — Foto: Rogério Júnior/g1

Cuiabá deve ter uma semana marcada por calor, céu nublado e pancadas de chuva, com possibilidade de trovoadas a partir desta segunda-feira (23) . A previsão do Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) indica que as precipitações podem ficar mais intensas na quinta (26) e na sexta-feira (27). A capital também está sob alerta amarelo para tempestades.

Nesta segunda-feira, os termômetros devem marcar entre 28°C e 36°C. Durante a manhã, o céu ficou com muitas nuvens e possibilidade de chuva isolada. À tarde e à noite, são esperadas pancadas de chuva, com possibilidade de precipitações isoladas.

Na terça-feira (24), o calor continua, com temperaturas entre 28°C e 36°C. A previsão aponta muitas nuvens e possibilidade de chuva isolada durante a manhã e a tarde. À noite, o céu deve permanecer encoberto. A umidade relativa do ar varia entre 50% e 80%.

Já na quarta-feira (25), a temperatura deve oscilar entre 27°C e 36°C. O céu permanece com muitas nuvens e há possibilidade de chuva isolada. A umidade pode chegar a 85%.

A previsão indica aumento das condições para chuva na quinta-feira (26), quando podem ocorrer pancadas acompanhadas de trovoadas isoladas. Os termômetros devem registrar mínima de 26°C e máxima de 35°C, com umidade relativa do ar entre 60% e 75%.

Na sexta-feira (27), o calor dá uma trégua, com temperaturas variando entre 25°C e 33°C. O dia deve ser de céu nublado, pancadas de chuva e possibilidade de trovoadas isoladas. A umidade relativa do ar pode chegar a 90%.

Veja como se proteger durante as tempestades

Diante da previsão de chuva e trovoadas, a orientação é redobrar os cuidados durante os períodos de instabilidade.

Entre as principais recomendações estão:

Evitar áreas abertas durante tempestades e não se abrigar debaixo de árvores.

Manter distância de postes, estruturas metálicas e placas de publicidade.

Não estacionar veículos próximos a árvores ou estruturas que possam cair.

Evitar utilizar aparelhos eletrônicos ligados à tomada durante as tempestades.

Não atravessar ruas ou áreas alagadas, mesmo que a água pareça pouco profunda.

A população também deve acompanhar os comunicados dos órgãos oficiais de meteorologia e da Defesa Civil.

articles.title: Corpo encontrado em Ubatuba após temporal; polícia investiga | G1
articles.standfirst: Prefeitura informou que a morte é investigada como uma possível vítima da enchente, mas ainda não há confirmação de que o caso tenha relação com as chuvas. Identidade da pessoa não foi divulgada.
articles.summary: O corpo foi localizado na região do Monte Valério após chuvas que deixaram desabrigados e suspenderam aulas em Ubatuba; a perícia apura as causas da morte.
articles.body:
Um corpo foi encontrado em um rio na região da Estrada Principal Monte Valério, na Ponte da Casanga, em Ubatuba (SP), na manhã desta segunda-feira (23), depois do temporal que provocou alagamentos e transbordamentos de rios na cidade.

A Prefeitura informou ao g1 que a morte está sendo investigada como uma possível vítima da enchente. No entanto, ainda não há confirmação de que a pessoa tenha morrido em decorrência das chuvas.

A Polícia Militar foi acionada às 6h47 para atender à ocorrência. Segundo informações iniciais, uma das hipóteses é de que uma pessoa de motocicleta foi tentar atravessar a correnteza, acabou arrastada pelo rio e morreu. No entanto, a dinâmica ainda depende de confirmação da perícia, que deve apontar as circunstâncias da ocorrência.

Até a última atualização desta reportagem, a identidade da vítima não havia sido divulgada. Também não foram informadas as circunstâncias em que o corpo foi encontrado.

O caso foi registrado em meio aos estragos provocados pela chuva que atingiu Ubatuba entre a noite de domingo (22) e a madrugada desta segunda. Segundo a Prefeitura, o município acumulou quase 172 milímetros de precipitação em apenas três horas. O volume provocou alagamentos em bairros, transbordamento de rios, quedas de árvores e deslizamentos de terra.

A situação também afetou o funcionamento de escolas municipais. Três unidades tiveram as aulas suspensas nesta segunda-feira: a Escola Municipal Altimira, no Itaguá; a Escola Municipal João Alexandre, no Sesmaria; e a Emei Alba, no Taquaral. A aplicação das provas do Sistema de Avaliação da Educação Básica do Estado de São Paulo (Saresp) também foi suspensa nas unidades afetadas.

Entre as regiões mais atingidas estão Sesmaria, Vila Rezende, Taquaral, Angelim e Itamambuca, além de áreas próximas aos rios Indaiá e Ressaca. No Sesmaria, o transbordamento de um rio atingiu imóveis. Um casal e duas crianças precisaram deixar a casa e foram para a residência de parentes.

Rua alagada no bairro Sumaré, em Ubatuba — Foto: Francisco Trevisan

Na Vila Rezende, moradores também precisaram sair de casa por causa da elevação do nível da água. A Defesa Civil mobilizou uma equipe com bote para ajudar no deslocamento de pessoas em áreas alagadas. Uma escola no Taquaral foi disponibilizada para receber temporariamente moradores da região.

A chuva também provocou queda de barreira na Estrada da Fortaleza, com comprometimento da rede elétrica. Uma árvore caiu nas proximidades do Prumirim e levou à interdição da Rodovia Rio-Santos (BR-101) por segurança. Houve ainda deslizamento na estrada de acesso à Ponta Grossa e pontos de alagamento em avenidas e vias de diferentes bairros.

Na manhã desta segunda, as equipes da Prefeitura e da Defesa Civil faziam um mutirão para limpar e liberar vias, organizar o trânsito e prestar assistência às famílias atingidas. O município deve fazer a distribuição de colchões, roupas de cama, materiais de higiene e limpeza e outros itens para os moradores.

Com maior volume de chuva do país em 24h, temporal deixa carros submersos, famílias desalojadas e estrada interditada em Ubatuba, SP — Foto: Divulgação/Defesa Civil de SP

A previsão divulgada pela Prefeitura indica que o tempo deve continuar instável nos próximos dias. A partir de quarta-feira (25), a aproximação de uma nova frente fria, combinada às altas temperaturas e à umidade na região, pode provocar pancadas de chuva com volumes mais expressivos, rajadas isoladas de vento e descargas elétricas, principalmente à tarde.

A Defesa Civil orienta moradores e turistas a evitar áreas alagadas, margens de rios e encostas durante períodos de chuva. Em caso de sinais de deslizamento ou elevação rápida do nível dos rios, a recomendação é deixar o local e acionar os órgãos de emergência.

US authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since 2024 over concerns that it smuggled Nvidia’s advanced artificial intelligence chips to China, Reuters reported.However, US officials have repeatedly said they have not reached a conclusion on whether Alice Huang spied for China. US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton reiterated that the matter remained under investigation.“Attorney General Blanche has been very clear that this is a matter under investigation, both Ms Huang and her company, for various matters,” Clayton told CNN’s State of the Union programme. “And I’m going to let that investigation play out.”The controversy intensified after an October 29 report by the New York Times, which triggered scrutiny of Jensen Huang’s personal and professional associations. articles.title: A woman bought a £4,550 Cartier bracelet from Harrods, returned it because it was too small and was denied a refund over alleged scratches; she represented herself in court and won £5,131
articles.summary: A woman who bought a £4,550 Cartier bracelet from Harrods has won a court battle against the luxury retailer after it refused to refund her, claiming the
articles.body: A woman who bought a £4,550 Cartier bracelet from Harrods has won a court battle against the luxury retailer after it refused to refund her, claiming the returned item had scratches. Georgia Romain, a hypnotherapist from Kingston upon Thames, had returned the 18-carat gold bracelet because it was too small for her wrist. However, after Harrods rejected her return and questioned the bracelet's condition, she challenged the decision in court without legal representation. Deputy District Judge Elaine Vignoli ruled that the retailer had failed to prove the bracelet was returned damaged, ordering Harrods to pay her £5,131, including interest and court fees.Harrods denied a refund for a £4,550 Cartier bracelet over alleged scratchesAfter receiving the bracelet, Harrods' customer service team rejected the return, claiming that the item had been damaged and had scratches on its surface. The retailer told Ms Romain that the bracelet would be transferred to its lost property department unless she reclaimed it within 30 days. The dispute centred on Harrods' claim that the alleged damage meant the 18-carat gold bangle could no longer be resold.According to The Independent, the retailer's customer service team had recorded a "pre-inspection video" of the bracelet after it was returned and examined. The video was used to identify what Harrods described as scratches and defects on the item's soft metal. However, Ms Romain questioned whether the bracelet shown in the footage was actually the one she had purchased, pointing out that the video did not show its unique serial number.Harrods told woman her rejected Cartier bracelet was legally her propertyAfter watching the video in August 2025, Ms Romain emailed Harrods to challenge the evidence being used to reject her return. She asked: "How can I be sure this is the same item because it doesn't show its unique serial number?" She also raised concerns about the appearance of the bracelet in the footage, saying that "the bracelet you’re holding in the pre-inspection video appears thicker than the one I ordered".However, the retailer's subsequent response did not address her concerns about the missing serial number or the video. Instead, Harrods informed her that the return had been "formally rejected" and that the bracelet "is legally now your property". Ms Romain subsequently brought a claim against the department store at Mayor's and City County Court, seeking a refund or replacement under the Consumer Contracts Regulations.Judge ruled Harrods failed to prove the returned Cartier bracelet had scratchesThe case was heard by Deputy District Judge Elaine Vignoli, who examined the evidence presented by both sides. Harrods' lawyers argued that the bracelet would have been "secured safely and handled carefully along the way". However, the judge questioned the lack of evidence supporting the retailer's account of how the item had been handled after it was returned.In her ruling, Judge Vignoli said: "For Harrods’ defence to succeed, I must be satisfied on the balance of probabilities that when they received the bracelet from Ms Romain it contained the same damage and the same scratches." She added: "But I am afraid there was a lack of evidence from the defendants before me today to satisfy me on that point." The judge subsequently determined that Harrods had not established that the bracelet was returned with scratches.Harrods failed to prove the scratched Cartier bracelet had lost its resale valueThe judge also questioned the department store's position that the alleged scratches had made the bracelet worthless. Harrods had argued that it could not resell the item because of its condition, but the court heard that the retailer had failed to provide solid evidence demonstrating how the alleged defects affected its value.According to The Independent, Judge Vignoli also challenged the retailer's argument over the bracelet's resale value, saying: "Harrods said that the bracelet is worth nothing to us because we can’t resell it, but I’m not quite sure I can agree with that – if it is genuinely worthless I would happily take it home with me." The judge described the bracelet as a "rather pretty, luxurious item" and concluded that the retailer's evidence had been insufficient.Harrods ordered to pay woman £5,131 after losing Cartier bracelet refund caseFollowing the ruling, Harrods was ordered to pay Ms Romain £4,550 for the returned bracelet. With accumulated interest and court fees, the total amount awarded came to £5,131. The judge concluded that the case had turned on the evidence presented and that the defendants had failed to substantiate their position.Judge Vignoli said: "This is a case which has turned very much on the evidence before the court and I am afraid to say that the defendants have been found wanting in this respect." She also stated that Harrods had "failed on the balance of probabilities" to prove that the bracelet had been returned with scratches.Woman vowed never to shop at Harrods after £5,131 court winSpeaking outside court after the decision, Ms Romain described herself as "very relieved" by the outcome. She also made clear that the experience had changed her attitude towards shopping at the department store, saying: "I’m never buying from Harrods again."She explained that she had spent years saving for the Cartier bracelet and had wanted to buy it as a birthday present for herself. "I was saving for years; I wanted to treat myself," she said. Reflecting on the outcome and the money she had spent, she added: "I’m going back to saving now. No more spending like this."Disclaimer: This article is based on information reported by The Independent and publicly available court proceedings. The Times of India has not independently verified the claims, evidence or circumstances surrounding the dispute between Georgia Romain and Harrods. The account of the court's findings and the compensation awarded is based on the reported proceedings and should not be interpreted as an independent confirmation by Harrods or its representatives.You use AI every day. articles.title: Dual storms threaten Thanksgiving plans from coast to coast
articles.summary: Heavy rain and wind could slow Thanksgiving travel along the East Coast and ground the balloons at Macy’s 100th parade, while unusually high tides threaten to flood roads around San Francisco Bay.
articles.body: Travelers across the Northeast have a window to beat the worst of the Thanksgiving weather before a coastal storm is expected to bring downpours and strong winds on Thanksgiving Day, potentially affecting the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. 🌧️ Track the storm in the CNN Weather app From Washington, DC, to Boston, dry weather is expected Tuesday and much of Wednesday, before the new system moves in. It’s the second seen along the East Coast in days, after heavy rain last week triggered flooding and disrupted travel on Florida’s Atlantic Coast. This week, a separate system will also pose trouble in the San Francisco Bay Area, where unusually high tides could flood shoreline roads Monday morning, even before the storm arrives Tuesday. The highest water is expected Wednesday morning, with authorities bracing for potential impacts to roads and infrastructure, including San Francisco International Airport. For anyone driving through the coastal Carolinas, Wednesday could also be a tough day on the road. A storm strengthening off the Southeast coast could bring downpours heavy enough to flood roads in parts of North and South Carolina. As it moves north, rain could reach Washington, DC, and Philadelphia by Wednesday night, setting up a wet drive along Interstate 95 Thanksgiving morning. How far inland the heaviest rain reaches will depend on how closely the storm hugs the coast. The Weather Prediction Center says 1 to 2 inches could fall along the I-95 corridor, with up to 3 inches possible in localized areas. Rain on Macy’s 100th parade? It’s the wind that could ground the balloons In New York City, the wind could put the giant balloons in the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in jeopardy even before the rain arrives. Winds are expected to strengthen Wednesday night, with widespread gusts of 35 to 45 mph forecast across the New York area Thursday and higher gusts near the coast. City rules call for grounding the giant balloons if sustained winds exceed 23 mph or gusts top 34 mph. The question is whether winds along the Manhattan parade route reach those speeds between the 8:30 a.m. start and noon finish. It’s too early to tell, as forecast details are still coming into focus. In Boston, the roughest weather is expected Thanksgiving Day into the evening. Wind-driven rain could slow drivers and strong gusts could delay flights at Logan International Airport. Along the Massachusetts coast, flooding is possible if the strongest onshore winds coincide with high tide. Travelers crossing the central Appalachians or driving through higher elevations in upstate New York and New England could encounter snow. How much of the powder will stick is still uncertain. The drive home should turn drier around Washington, DC, by Friday, though it could still be gusty in spots. Rain and snow showers could linger into Saturday in northern New England. Forecasters are also watching for a separate storm that could form off the East Coast over the weekend, but it’s too early to say whether it would affect Sunday travel. High tides threaten Bay Area roads before the rain arrives While this Monday looks mostly dry in San Francisco, the National Weather Service expects several road closures along the low-lying shores of San Francisco and San Pablo bays this week as king tides return. A coastal flood warning runs from early Monday through Thanksgiving Day, with the greatest threat around each morning’s high tide. Wednesday morning is the time to watch. Water at the San Francisco tide gauge could come within an inch of its 1983 record close to 11 a.m. PT. High tide can arrive up to 90 minutes later elsewhere in the bay. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie has urged residents to avoid nonessential travel from Monday afternoon through Wednesday afternoon. Both San Francisco and Oakland airports have been preparing for the high water. San Francisco International Airport has staged sandbags and portable flood barriers and checked its pumps. For travelers flying out of Oakland, airport officials recommend using Hegenberger Road or 98th Avenue, the two main access routes, which they say are outside the reach of tidal flooding. Rain and gusty winds will arrive in the Bay Area Tuesday and continue into Wednesday. Much of the region could pick up a quarter-inch to an inch of rain, with 1 to 2 inches in the North Bay. Gusts could reach 40 mph along the coast and through some mountain passes. Farther north, drivers along the Oregon and Washington coasts could face heavy rain Wednesday and more wet weather on Thanksgiving.

articles.title: What six grazing horses tell us about England's housing crisis
articles.summary: ⁠In Middlesbrough, York and Kent, the BBC sees why successive governments have failed to build enough homes.
articles.body:
About a five-minute walk from the train station in Middlesbrough, six horses are grazing lazily on a derelict patch of land.

Tethered and friendly, the animals do not attract much attention from residents, despite being so close to the town centre.

But their presence on the land, by the banks of the River Tees, is a symbol of the UK's decades-long failure to build enough houses.

In 2004, the local council announced plans to build 2,400 homes on the grass the horses are eating.

But 22 years later, just 216 homes have been built. The money initially outlined for the project has never been found.

The UK is in a housing crisis with demand for homes continuing to outstrip supply.

To understand why successive governments have failed to build enough houses, BBC News went to this Middlesbrough scheme, and planned developments in York and the Isle of Sheppey, in Kent.

Each has its own story, with finances, infrastructure planning and developers' appetites all playing a major role - issues mirrored at other sites across the country.

Combined, the projects we visited promised to build 7,400 homes. To date, just 326 have been constructed.

Shortfalls like this affect national goals significantly, says Anthony Breach, director of policy and research at the Centre for Cities think tank.

The UK's reliance on "large, complex schemes" to deliver new housing means that "when our larger sites get a bit stuck, that has a disproportionate impact on national housebuilding", he says.

These large-scale projects, increasingly favoured by private developers and often driven by local councils, are key to the Labour government's target of building 1.5 million homes in England by the next election.

The 2004 plans for Middlehaven in Middlesbrough, a long-disused industrial site, included not just thousands of homes but also a theatre, restaurants and hotels.

It was billed as a £500m development, but it had one fundamental flaw: the money never existed.

Instead, this figure was simply an estimate of overall cost, Middlesbrough Council told us.

Almost a decade later, in 2013, the development was proposed again. This time, the council bought 185 homes that already existed, so they could be demolished to make space.

Yet only 216 homes have been built to replace them, a net gain of 31.

The council says delivery of the masterplan was curtailed by the 2008 financial crash, "leading to the departure of the council's development partner".

A college campus, business space and housing have been delivered, it says, and a new school is being built.

The price that new homes will sell for is a key factor in large developments progressing, says Breach, as housebuilding firms look for returns on their investments.

In places where house prices are lower, he says, public sector funds may be needed to "bridge the gap between the cost of building [works] and the price at which the houses can be sold for".

In September, Middlesbrough Council announced plans for 462 new homes on the site - the beginning, it hopes, of a development of 3,400 homes in all.

This time, however, the council is far more cautious, acknowledging the money might not be there to achieve everything it would like.

In York, a plan for 3,000 homes was announced in 2001, but a quarter of a century later, not a single house has been built.

Alongside the homes, close to the historic centre of the city, were to be business and hospitality opportunities - just like in Middlesbrough.

Planning consultant Nora Galley was hired by the local council to develop the York Central masterplan.

Her designs, she tells the BBC, combined a realistic vision with a plan to deliver it.

"It wasn't just a beautiful place that looked great in architect's drawings," she says.

But by the time the 2008 crash hit, work had not begun.

In September this year, the project's first phase was finally given the green light, with some 2,500 homes planned to be built by 2040.

Galley is disappointed that construction has taken so long to get under way, and that fewer homes will be built than originally planned.

"There is no fabric in this country to manage the delivery of strategic projects," she tells us - highlighting what she sees as supply chain issues and a lack of construction training.

In June, trade body the Construction Industry Training Board backed Galley's point - citing a need for 206,000 new construction workers across the UK between now and 2030.

York Central is now set to cost £2bn to complete, far more than the hundreds of millions of pounds local papers reported when plans were first set out.

Delays to the project have cost York greatly, says Galley. The city has missed out on "wealth, opportunities, a better-performing economy".

Residents we spoke to were largely in favour of York Central, seeing its potential. But all seemed puzzled by the amount of time it had taken.

Cycle lanes, pristine paths and bus stops surround the site, yet nobody was around to use them. "I had colour in my hair when they first announced it," quips one middle-aged woman who lives in the neighbouring estate.

The main problem has been the site's positioning, surrounded by railway lines, says Labour leader of City of York Council, Claire Douglas.

The project stalled because, for a time, there was no money from government to pay for an access road allowing construction materials on to the site, she says.

But now the access road is nearing completion and the first houses should be built within two years, she says.

Nearly 200 miles (322km) south, on the Isle of Sheppey in Kent, a planned development of up to 2,000 new homes was meant to help regenerate a deprived part of the island.

It is now 23 years since the plan was initially conceived, and 17 years since it was backed by local councils. But only 110 houses have been built.

The project was hailed in a 2009 press release as a "£400m regeneration" of the area, but Swale Borough Council has told the BBC that, as in Middlesbrough, the money never actually existed.

The figure, it said, was an estimation "of the likely investment required to deliver the scheme at that time", and there was no housing developer lined up.

Some 3,000 jobs were also expected to be created, but only some have materialised.

A retail park housing a Morrisons, Burger King and Sports Direct among other outlets has been completed, but plans for a marina have been scrapped.

Where the hundreds of homes should stand is an empty field surrounded by metal railings. Locals say the grass is occasionally mowed.

Meanwhile, the council has 1,800 households waiting for social housing.

"We do need a few more houses [here], but we also need more doctors and things like that as well," says Marie Miller, lifelong resident of the neighbouring village of Rushenden.

The planned "state of the art" healthcare centre on the same site remains unbuilt.

Nothing has happened on the site in a long time, Miller says.

The original 2,000-homes plan was scaled back in 2015 to 1,180, but even this reduced figure is unlikely to be achieved. According to council documents, the project is back at the planning stage.

Homes England, the government's housing and regeneration agency, is now approaching housebuilders for their "early observations" about developing the site.

After the economic downturn of 2008, the planned level of development "proved to be an optimistic forecast", the local council said, adding it was "working closely with Homes England to agree an updated timescale".

These three schemes we have visited are not the only projects to have failed to deliver new housing over long time periods.

In London, where housebuilding has fallen substantially in recent years, not one of the 3,500 homes planned for Convoy's Wharf in Deptford has been built - despite outline planning permission being given in 2005. Planning problems and objections from locals have contributed to the delays.

On the north side of the Thames, a 2008 plan to build 10,800 units at Barking Riverside was stalled for years because of poor transport links. However, since the creation of a new rail line, 3,000 homes now have been built and plans have been approved to almost double the housing development to 20,000 homes.

The glacial speed at which things get done, particularly at the sites we visited in Middlesbrough, York and Kent, offer key insights as to why the UK has not built as many homes as it needs.

Part of the housebuilding challenge, says Anthony Breach from Centre for Cities, is that the UK's planning system is "pretty unusual internationally".

Even if a developer follows all the rules "you can still be denied planning permission by local politicians", he says - meaning developments take much longer, and risk being upended if a new party is elected locally.

To overcome planning delays, mayoral development corporations (MDCs) are increasingly being established by England's regional mayors. These bodies can take planning duties away from a local authority and make compulsory land purchases, enabling large-scale projects to move more quickly.

Breach sees this as a positive step, describing MDCs as a shortcut through the planning system that should see housebuilding increase.

A spokesperson for the Ministry of Housing told the BBC it was "working with Homes England to get stalled schemes moving, with housing starts up 20% on this time last year".

They added: "We've unblocked and accelerated more than 130,000 homes and, through our planning overhaul and £40bn Social and Affordable Homes Programme, we are unlocking development and building the homes our country needs."

The schemes in Middlesbrough, York and Kent may eventually come good - but decades later than promised, their failures all contributing to the UK's chronic lack of housing.

articles.title: Folkestone homelessness exhibition to run until 17 December
articles.summary: Shane Record says his exhibition shows that art "can have a positive impact upon its community".
articles.body:
A Kent artist who has painted six portraits of people facing homelessness says an ongoing exhibition is a chance to "give these people more visibility".

Shane Record, who has been a fixture in the Folkestone art scene for more than 20 years, met the people he would later paint through his passion for baking.

He told BBC Radio Kent: "About four or five years ago, my children were a little bit younger and we had this Sunday ritual of me baking cinnamon rolls for them...they loved it so much that they said, 'Dad, you should make extra and share them out.'"

Record said sharing his baked goods with those facing homelessness "led to friendships being made" and him "learning about their lives".

A man called Jamie, who Record really "warmed to" as he had the same childhood name, inspired the artist to paint the portraits.

Sadly, he died before the painting started.

"He [Jamie] lived right next to my house in a tent, and he went to bed one night and didn't get out of it. It was terribly sad," Record said.

The artist went on to paint five portraits of Raheem, Clive, Jo, Karen, and Rob in oil paints.

Matty, the final portrait, was painted in water on coloured paper which allowed Record to use a technique which saw the image disappear once dry.

This was to highlight the higher mortality rate of people facing homelessness.

Record said 15% of the proceeds from the ongoing exhibition at the House of Afsana Gallery will go towards local homeless support service Rainbow Centre and the Big Issue.

The artist believes this shows his "long-held belief that art can have a positive and direct impact upon its community".

"It's very important to me to continually prove that," he said.

As for those he painted, Record is grateful that they all "trusted me enough to do this".

The exhibition, which opened on Friday, was scheduled to run until 17 December.

articles.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine was behind drone attacks on Russian ships off Libya
articles.summary: President Zelenskyy says Ukrainian forces sank the Russian warship Merkury in an “exemplary” sea drone operation.
articles.body:
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Ukrainian forces sank ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠a Russian warship in Benghazi and also hit a cargo ship used to transport weapons off the coast of Libya, hailing an “exemplary Ukrainian operation in response to Russia’s war”.

Ukraine’s president said in a statement on Monday that the Merkury, one of Russia’s newest warships, sank after Ukrainian forces launched seven naval drones on Sunday. A KA-27 combat helicopter was also destroyed in the attack.

He confirmed that Ukraine’s forces also attacked the cargo ship Angara. Libya’s eastern health ministry in Benghazi said all crew members from the cargo ship had been rescued and were receiving treatment after Sunday’s attack.

Authorities in eastern Libya said the warship was docked in the port of Benghazi when the explosion occurred.

“We firmly reject the use of our territory or territorial waters as an arena for settling scores or as an extension of external conflicts,” Saddam Haftar, the deputy commander-in-chief of the eastern Libyan administration’s forces said.

“The security and sovereignty of Libya are a national responsibility that leaves no room for political posturing or the exploitation of incidents to propagate accusations and incite fear,” he said.

Reporting from Moscow, Al Jazeera’s Yulia Shapovalova said that Russian authorities have not yet made an official comment on the drone attack on the warship.

“According to the Libyan side, the ship was returning to Russia from its mission and stopped in Benghazi for refuelling,” our correspondent said. She said it was not clear if there were any casualties.

“Russian military infrastructure is Ukraine’s target, not just in Russia, but pretty much throughout the world,” she said.

The United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) expressed “serious concern” over the drone attacks , calling for “an immediate, independent and transparent investigation”.

“Libya cannot afford and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts,” UNSMIL wrote on X.

The eastern administration did not identify who was behind Sunday’s attack but said Libya was “not a party to the Russian-Ukrainian war”.

The oil-rich nation of Libya has been divided between the government in Tripoli and a rival administration in the east since the overthrow of longtime ruler Muammar Gaddafi in 2011.

articles.title: After Etsy changed its terms to permit AI training using sellers' content, longtime artists began shutting their online shops; the company has now promised to rewrite the policy following the backlash
articles.summary: Several longtime sellers on Etsy have started closing their online shops after the marketplace introduced new terms allowing sellers' content to be used
articles.body: Several longtime sellers on Etsy have started closing their online shops after the marketplace introduced new terms allowing sellers' content to be used for artificial intelligence (AI) development. The decision has upset artists and small business owners, who fear their original work could be used by AI companies without their permission.The revised terms, which are scheduled to take effect on December 16, allow Etsy and its "third party partners and vendors" to use sellers' content to develop, train, test and improve AI and machine learning technologies. The company says these tools will help improve the marketplace and make it safer for users.However, sellers are concerned about the broad permission given to outside companies. According to The Inquirer, some have decided to leave a platform they had used for years rather than accept the new conditions. Following the protests, Etsy has promised to rewrite the policy and provide a clearer explanation of how sellers' work may be used.Artists shut shops after policy changeIllustrator Aaron Millard was among those who decided to leave. He announced on Instagram last week that he was deleting the Etsy shop he had operated for nearly a decade.Millard objected to the possibility of his artwork being used to train AI systems and shared with third parties. He also criticised the absence of an option for sellers to refuse such use. "My work took years to learn and create. I won’t let it be stolen," he wrote.Kristen and Geoff Zephyrus, founders of home goods and stationery brand Cognitive Surplus, also removed their shop after selling through Etsy for 13 years. In an Instagram post last Thursday, they criticised the company's approach to sellers' creative work and the possibility of third parties benefiting from it.Kristen Zephyrus explained their decision in an interview on Friday. "For Etsy to be helping to train algorithms with our human content is just unimaginably awful," she said. "We don’t want anything to do with that."Etsy says it will protect human creativityEtsy has defended the revised policy, saying the intention is not to use artists' work to reproduce their creations through AI.James Ossman, the company's vice president for customer operations, addressed sellers in a statement published on Etsy's website earlier this week. He said the company would not use their content to train AI models designed to copy original work or replace human creativity.Ossman cited fraud detection tools and advertising on the platform as reasons for allowing third parties to access sellers' content.However, the explanation has not prevented criticism of the revised terms. Sellers remain concerned about the extent of permission being granted and how their work could be used outside the marketplace.In an email to The New York Times on Friday, Ossman said Etsy was working to make the wording clearer and would share revised terms directly with sellers soon."We’ve heard sellers’ concerns about the updated terms, and we should have done more to explain how we use their content to help buyers discover their work, support their businesses and keep Etsy safe," he wrote.He also stressed that creators retained ownership of their work, adding, "Their creative work belongs to them."Etsy has faced seller protests beforeFounded in 2005, Etsy was created to help independent artisans find customers online. However, disagreements over company policies have previously led to protests from its seller community.In 2022, more than 20,000 sellers went on strike after Etsy increased its basic sales fee from 5% to 6.5%, marking a 30% rise.The company also faced complaints in October over the growing presence of low-quality AI-generated content, commonly described by users as "AI slop". Etsy subsequently announced tighter restrictions on such material.The latest dispute comes as several internet companies face pressure to adopt AI while dealing with concerns from users who oppose the technology's use. A Gallup poll conducted during the summer found that nearly 40% of Americans believed AI did more harm than good.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Widowed amid war and displacement: Sudanese mothers struggle to survive
articles.summary: War widows in Sudan face growing challenges supporting their children as the cost of living increases.
articles.body:
Warning: This story contains descriptions of sexual assault that some readers may find disturbing.

Port Sudan, Sudan – In Sudan’s displacement camps, the stories of residents often follow similar paths, but each loss and hardship is a deeply personal experience.

Arafa Abdelaziz endured a dangerous 15-day journey from Omdurman to a displacement camp in Port Sudan in late 2023, after losing her husband and one of her two sons, who died early in the war.

Her husband died just days after fighting broke out between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in April 2023, leaving her to care for her remaining two children as their home city of Omdurman in Khartoum State came under bombardment.

Five months later, her eight-year-old son was killed by a stray bullet during clashes near Omdurman’s market.

“My son was playing outside the house with his friends when I suddenly heard a loud noise. When I went outside, I found that his head had been shattered by gunfire,” said the 33-year-old.

With the fighting between the SAF and RSF continuing in Omdurman, one of the centres of the power struggle between the two former allies at the start of the war, Arafa eventually decided to flee the city with her six-year-old son, who has a brain condition affecting his development.

She describes the journey to Port Sudan as a prolonged and horrifying ordeal. Near Jebel Aulia, south of Khartoum, RSF fighters intercepted the vehicle they were in and the passengers were robbed and assaulted.

“They asked every woman carrying a child how she wanted her son to be killed. I told them to kill me before they touched my son,” Arafa recalled.

When she confronted the fighters as they attempted to assault her child, one of them hit her with the butt of his rifle, leaving her unconscious for more than an hour.

“When I regained consciousness, I saw RSF fighters raping the young women who were travelling with us on the bus. Some were raped in front of their fathers. I felt it was the end,” she said.

In October 2026, UN Women reported that 12.7 million people, mostly women and girls, needed support for gender-based violence in Sudan – four times the pre-war figure.

The agency warned that sexual violence is being used as a weapon of war, with women and girls at risk while fleeing areas of fighting, in displacement camps and while searching for food, water and shelter.

Arafa said her greatest fear throughout the ordeal was for her younger son’s safety. When the fighters asked what valuables she had, she told them she owned nothing. They took two gold rings from her fingers and after severely beating her, let her continue her journey.

“I arrived in Port Sudan with nothing, having lost my husband. My son’s condition had worsened because of what we went through on the journey and because he could not receive his medication regularly,” she said.

It was Arafa’s first time in Port Sudan, so, having no family or friends there to support her, she headed to a school sheltering displaced families. She was later transferred to another displacement camp, where she now lives with her son. But reaching relative safety was not the end of her struggles. Her son’s condition fluctuates, and she remains worried about his health and future.

“Sometimes he imagines strange things because of his illness,” she said. “Yesterday, he told me he could see a lot of blood on the ground. It makes me think every day about his future with this condition.”

Arafa cannot afford his medication, so she has resorted to giving him medicine only when his condition deteriorates. She depends largely on aid distributed in the camp, as her needs and those of her son continue to grow.

“I’m afraid to leave him alone at home, out of my sight, in case he has a seizure or hurts himself,” she said.

The war in Sudan has killed as many as 150,000 people and forced millions from their homes, often to camps in impoverished neighbouring countries.

Income levels have dropped to 1992 levels and extreme poverty rates are worse than in the 1980s, according to the United Nations. Due to conscription, fatalities and emigration to other regions and countries for work, women have become the sole guardians in many displaced Sudanese households.

The UN’s 2025 Gender Snapshot found that 75 percent of female-headed households in Sudan were food insecure – three times the rate among male-headed households.

The Mashad Observatory has documented 72,202 cases of widowhood since the outbreak of war in Sudan in April 2023. That constitutes a complex humanitarian crisis which can lead to the collapse of household incomes, stability and protection systems. In the long term, it means transmitting deprivation, economic vulnerability and psychological trauma from one generation to the next.

These cumulative impacts can weaken social cohesion, exacerbate inequalities and undermine the capacity of local communities to recover from the consequences of war. This growing burden means fewer opportunities for women to work and increased dependence on humanitarian assistance, with long-term economic implications for Sudan, the group said.

“Their suffering is further compounded when women lose the primary source of household income or are forced to abandon their homes and communities without adequate financial resources or social support networks. Such circumstances may expose them to heightened risks of economic exploitation, gender-based violence, forced or early marriage involving their daughters and the interruption of their children’s education,” a spokesperson for the organisation told Al Jazeera.

“These pressures may also contribute to deteriorating mental health as a result of cumulative trauma, overwhelming responsibilities and the absence of appropriate psychosocial support services.”

With humanitarian agencies saying that Sudan’s 2026 response plan, which aims to reach 20.4 million people and requires $2.9bn, has received only 47% of the funding needed, there will be challenges in providing these families with the necessary support.

“Addressing this challenge therefore requires a transition from temporary emergency relief towards a comprehensive national strategy that places widows and female-headed households at the centre of Sudan’s recovery and reconstruction plans,” said the organisation.

“Such a strategy should include sustainable cash assistance, economic empowerment programmes, vocational training, access to decent employment, improved access to finance and productive enterprises, as well as guaranteed access to education, healthcare, legal protection and psychosocial support.”

Zahra Idris, 39, fled Khartoum with her husband and two children as shelling intensified, arriving in Port Sudan three years ago.

Her husband initially rented a house in the working-class neighbourhood of Al-Kasara. But when they could no longer afford the rent, the landlord evicted them. The family moved to a school shelter before being relocated to a displacement camp at the start of the school year.

Two months ago, Zahra’s husband died of heart disease, leaving her to care for their two children with little support beyond humanitarian assistance, which has become increasingly limited.

“Since my husband died, my fears have grown. I cannot go out to look for work until I complete the mourning period prescribed in Islam, which lasts four months and ten days,” she said.

Her 12-year-old son has an intellectual disability and requires regular medical care, something the family cannot afford given the rising cost of living.

“There is no one to help me. I just want my son’s condition to improve enough for him to attend a school for children with disabilities,” she said.

“Going from one organisation to another, looking for someone to cover my son’s medical treatment and education, cost me around 100,000 Sudanese pounds. That money could have covered our household needs for several days.”

articles.title: Father and daughter detained by ICE at Seattle airport were traveling to family baptism, lawyer says
articles.summary: A father and daughter detained by masked immigration officers on an airport jet bridge in Seattle, causing chaos in front of other passengers, were heading to a family baptism ceremony in California, their lawyer said Sunday.
articles.body: A father and daughter detained by masked immigration officers on an airport jet bridge in Seattle, causing chaos in front of other passengers, were heading to a family baptism ceremony in California, their lawyer said Sunday. Other passengers boarding the Alaska Airlines flight at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport on Saturday used their cellphones to film the father and daughter being detained by the officers, who were wearing unmarked jackets and khaki pants. The recordings were widely viewed on social media. The videos show the officers struggling with someone on the ground. The flight, bound for Los Angeles, was delayed. The father and daughter were traveling to attend a baptism ceremony in California and are seeking asylum in the U.S., where they have lived since 2015, their lawyer, Olia Catala, told The Associated Press in a telephone interview. They have no criminal record, Catala said. “They’ve done everything correctly, and these are educated people,” Catala said of the father and daughter. “She went to college, to university, she worked for a nonprofit. No criminal history (for) any of them. So it’s just heartbreaking.” Immigration and Customs Enforcement said in a statement that its officers detained Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, an immigrant from Mexico who it said had overstayed his visa “in violation of our nation’s laws.” During the confrontation, another passenger “hurled hot coffee on the officers,” the ICE statement said. That woman, Sofia Hernandez Mejia, was determined to be in the U.S. illegally from Mexico and to have also overstayed her visa, ICE said. She could be charged with assaulting a federal officer. Mejia, in her mid-20s, had married a U.S. citizen and filed paperwork for adjustment of her status, her attorney said. Mejia’s husband was accompanying Mejia and her father when they were detained Saturday, Catala added. The husband was not detained, the attorney said. Both were being held at the Northwest ICE Processing Center in Tacoma, Catala said. She said Mejia was carrying a cup of coffee when the confrontation occurred. “When somebody’s charging at you, you’re going to drop a cup of coffee,” Catala said. “It was just a lot of commotion, and honestly, if somebody is running at you or charging at you and they’re not wearing a uniform, you don’t know who they are,” Catala said. “There was a lot of panic, chaos, not knowing what’s going on.” “They just lunged forward. They didn’t identify themselves and then sort of hit this family from behind,” John Gaedeke, who was in line waiting to board the flight and filmed part of the confrontation on his cellphone, said of the officers. Gaedeke said passengers on the jet bridge were screaming or crying “because it was just so emotional, and just to see the pain and anguish and then the speed and violence with which it happened.” Alaska Airlines said ICE officers gave no advance notice of the enforcement action, which occurred during a busy travel weekend ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. ICE has stepped up arrests at airports since the summer, especially targeting people it says have overstayed visas. Alaska Airlines said it was working with the Port of Seattle, which manages the airport, to see if protocols were followed, and also that it has raised concerns “directly with the appropriate authorities.” The Port of Seattle said in a statement that the arrest was distressing not only for the affected family but for other passengers, and that local authorities would “engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred.” Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson, a Democrat, said ICE’s tactics were “deeply un-American” and called for the agency’s abolition. “The video is horrific and it is chilling,” Ferguson said at a news conference Saturday with labor leaders and local elected officials.
